correctness.rationale: The greedy period-embedding lemma follows by an exact weak-descent argument. Mirrored pairs contribute t+e weak descents in either parity, and the first-half equality positions give an injective count. Bivariate generating functions follow by summing minimum required periods; recurrence and asymptotic root follow algebraically. The fully attached code checks independent brute-force/DP computations for 17 small exhaustive cases and 138 larger cells, not as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact arbitrary-alphabet length spectrum and bivariate generating function, not the already known binary alternating longest-subsequence length. Compared original 2019, 2024, and 2025 full texts by statement and implication; none states or directly implies the whole exact spectrum. The 2017 automaton full text was inaccessible, so possible hidden stronger coverage is explicitly a material risk. Published-record searches found no dominating/equivalent spectrum.

It is a natural benchmark for palindromic subsequence automata and distinct-count algorithms, beyond ordinary longest-subsequence observations.
